result.question: Give me a sample-by-sample picture of the fault gases in Transformer 1 at MAIN between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. For each sample, list hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene and acetylene. Name the dominant gas, meaning the one with the highest ppm, and give its percentage of the five-gas total. Then tell me whether the dominant gas changed at any point in the window. Say what that shift points to, for example hydrogen pointing to partial discharge, ethylene to a hotter thermal fault, or acetylene to arcing. Also rank the five gases by their percentage growth from the first to the last sample. If a gas is null in a sample, leave it out of that sample's total and mark it as missing. If fewer than two samples have all five gases, give the ranking from the latest reading alone and say that no trend could be established.

| Timestamp | H2 | CH4 | C2H6 | C2H4 | C2H2 | 5-gas total | Dominant gas | % of total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2024-01-15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32409 | Ethylene | 51.48% |
| 2024-01-16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 32056 | Ethylene | 51.47% |
| 2024-01-17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 32308 | Ethylene | 51.69% |
| 2024-01-18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 32307 | Ethylene | 51.37% |

No gases were null in any sample; all 4 samples have the full set.

## Dominant gas shift
**No shift** — ethylene is dominant in every sample, consistently ~51.5% of the five-gas total. Ethylene at these very high concentrations (16,500–16,700 ppm) points to a **high-temperature thermal fault** (hot metal, roughly >700 °C per IEC 60599). The very low acetylene (6–8 ppm) argues against arcing, and hydrogen at only ~2,850 ppm (well below ethylene) argues against partial discharge as the primary mechanism.

## Percentage growth ranking (first → last sample, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-18)
1. **Hydrogen: +1.93%** (2845 → 2900)
2. **Acetylene: 0.00%** (7 → 7)
3. **Ethylene: −0.50%** (16684 → 16600)
4. **Ethane: −0.31%** (5467 → 5450)
5. **Methane: −0.76%** (7406 → 7350)

(Strict ranking by magnitude of growth: H2 grew the most; ethane declined slightly less than methane.)

**Overall picture:** a stable, severe thermal-in-oil condition dominated by ethylene, with essentially flat concentrations over the window — no acute change or new fault mode emerging in these four days, but the absolute levels warrant close monitoring/inspection.
